name: WS2813B-V5
title: WS2813B-V5/W: addressable RGB LED in a 5050 SMD package, with a built-in driver and a backup data line
summary: A top-emitting 5050 surface-mount RGB LED with its own control chip inside, so each package is one individually addressable full-colour light point. It takes a single-wire serial stream at up to 800 Kbps, keeps the first 24 bits (8 bits each for green, red and blue, 256 levels per colour) and passes the rest on, regenerated, from its DO pin to the next device. A second data path (BIN in, BO out) lets the chain keep running past one failed device. It runs from 5 V, drives the three dice at a constant current with a refresh rate of 2 kHz, survives a reversed supply, and needs no parts around it, not even a decoupling capacitor.

notes: WS2813B-V5/W is the WS2813B-V5 with a misted encapsulant; the /W suffix came with that change.
The V5 driver has stronger internal filtering than V4 and no capacitor inside the package.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A string of n devices on one 5 V supply and ground. The controller drives DI into the first device's DIN and BI into its BIN. Each device's DO goes to the next DIN and its BO to the next BIN, so both data paths run in series down the string; the last device's DO and BO are brought out as the outputs DO and BO. Nothing else is fitted.

parts.note: last of the string; any number of further devices sit between L2 and Ln, wired the same way

where.256: grey levels of each of the red, green and blue channels

equations.expr: T0H + T0L ≥ 1.25 µs; T1H + T1L ≥ 1.25 µs

where.T0H, T0L: high and low times of a 0 bit
where.T1H, T1L: high and low times of a 1 bit

operation.text: Data arrives on one line in single-wire NZR code, one bit per pulse: a short high pulse is a 0 and a long one a 1 (timing in the data transfer table). After power-on reset each device takes the first 24 bits it sees on DIN into its latch and sends everything after them out of DO, regenerated, so the stream reaching the next device is 24 bits shorter. A low level held longer than 280 µs ends the frame; the long reset time keeps short gaps in the stream from being taken as a reset, which suits slow, low-cost microcontrollers.

In one refresh cycle the controller sends 24 bits per device back to back, first device first, then holds the line low for more than 280 µs. Each later device in the string sees the same stream with the data of the devices ahead of it removed.

Besides DIN and DO each device has a second data path, BIN to BO. With both lines run down the string, a single device that fails does not stop the data from reaching the devices after it, nor the light from the rest of the string.

Every device reshapes the data before passing it on, so the waveform does not degrade along the string and the number of devices is limited only by the data rate, not by signal quality. The rate is up to 800 Kbps; at 30 frames per second at least 1024 devices can be driven. Two devices may be more than 2 m apart with no extra circuitry between them.

An internal precision oscillator and a programmable constant-current stage drive the red, green and blue dice, which gives consistent colour from device to device. Each channel has 256 grey levels, and the refresh rate is 2 KHz, low enough in flicker that HD video cameras show none.
Connecting the 5 V supply the wrong way round does not damage the device.
No external components are needed, including a supply capacitor.

The lens is modified epoxy resin, which collects dust readily; dust does not lower brightness, but assembled LEDs are kept in a clean container. Organic solvents are to be avoided, and any cleaning fluid is checked first for whether it attacks the resin. Ultrasonic cleaning is not used; where there is no alternative, its power, the bake time and the assembly conditions have to be evaluated first.

The LED is moisture sensitive, MSL 5a, and ships in an aluminium foil bag with desiccant; that bag protects it for only about 1 to 2 months. Moisture taken up can expand in reflow and lift the resin off the lead frame. Before SMT, the opened reel is baked at 70 to 75 ℃ for 24 h or more. From leaving the oven to the end of all high-temperature steps (reflow, dip, wave soldering, rework heating) is at most 24 h at under 30 ℃ and 60 %RH. Placement follows paste printing within about 1 h. Loose parts left in air for a long time (surplus, machine rejects, repair stock) are baked again: a whole reel at 70 to 75 ℃ for 24 h or more, loose parts at 120 ℃ for 4 h.

Pick the LED up by its sides. Do not press the lens with fingers or sharp tools, and do not stack boards or parts on top of one another; either can damage the circuit inside. Do not store or use the LED in acidic surroundings (pH below 7).
